facts: The current in-memory TurnAffinity cache persists only completion_text plus usage/provider affinity metadata, not the rendered OpenAI Responses payload.
On a cache hit, handle_openai_responses calls responses_payload(completion_text, ...) again.
responses_payload creates new random response_id, tool call_id, and output item id with uuid.uuid4() on each rendering.
Therefore two cache renders of the same semantic tool recommendation produce different protocol identities even without a process restart.
risk: For tool-producing Responses, semantic text caching is not an idempotent protocol replay. A client retry can receive a new call_id for the same already-planned action. Combined with the separately reproduced post-restart exact-replay fallback, this means durable recovery must preserve the rendered Responses result or deterministically preserve its protocol identities; storing only completion_text is insufficient.
acceptance_direction: Persist/replay the exact rendered Responses result required for a completed request, including response/output item/call IDs and enough usage/model metadata to reproduce both non-streaming and SSE completion without provider inference.
Bind the replay record to a content-free exact request fingerprint plus conversation/turn identity and lifecycle/version boundary.
Publish the replay record atomically with conversation progress so a crash cannot leave provider progress marked durable while the matching response replay is absent.
Until that atomic durable replay exists, the prepared 409 fail-closed exact-replay guard is the safety floor and is preferable to silently re-planning an already processed tool result.
